Short answer: Choose Squarespace when the owner wants a straightforward all-in-one editor. Choose Webflow when the site needs more structured content or design control and someone will own the setup and care.

What this means for your business

Both can publish a serious business site. The real difference is who edits it, how often the structure changes, what integrations must work, and what leaving later looks like.

What to watch

  • A site too complicated for the person updating it.
  • Plan, workspace, add-on, and scheduling costs mixed together.
  • A migration promise that ignores forms, bookings, analytics, or redirects.
  • Nobody named as the account and domain owner.

Do this next

  1. List the pages and repeated content you need.
  2. Have the future editor change a service, photo, and hour.
  3. Price the plan and add-ons needed for launch.
  4. Write down domain, export, redirect, and handoff requirements.

When Little Fight fits

We build around the business, including custom work when a builder is the wrong fit. If either platform handles the job cleanly, we will say so.
